notes: Preset PvE Shooter kept whole, but its spawner-npc is written for hostile AI entering a fight; here it means shoppers walking in the door. The shoppers are targets, not threats, and nothing attacks the player.
Bodies persist where they fall, so aisle width has to allow a walkable route past lying shoppers rather than being sized only for standing crowd flow.
Whole map is a single interior; P3 covers the store-to-car-park threshold if the entrance is included, and drops to P0 if the build starts inside.

notes_for_us: Shooter has no row for a target that is not an enemy. npc-population is who lives here and spawner-npc is where hostiles enter; this prompt's shoppers are the things you shoot and also the ambient crowd, and the two rows are defined against each other specifically so they cannot be the same thing.

Every one of Shooter's nine presets is a competitive mode or a firing range. A game with no opponent, no scoring and no threat has to borrow PvE Shooter and then reject its central option, which the brief made visible but the skill would not have.

The prompt renames the setting - 'a Walmart, but call it Tops Supermarket'. The rename is both a metadata fact and a piece of geometry to draw on the storefront, and nothing in the handoff distinguishes those, so the sign shipped as free text.

notes_for_us: Mirrors have no option and a dress-up game is mostly mirrors. In a genre whose entire subject is looking at your own avatar, the reflective surface that makes the room work has to ship as free text with no route, next to a runway that is baked invisibly into the shape.

Four zones were named - dressing area, mirrors, runway, photo booth - and only one of them, the photo booth, had an option to land on. The emit block has no way to say 'the map is these four rooms in this relationship'; it is a flat list of picks plus one shape name.

This prompt describes its environment in more detail than anything else in my batch and still comes out with three free-text entries out of five. The gap is not obscure requests, it is ordinary interior furniture.
